assumptions.assumption: The reviewer calls `get_reviewer_instructions` because prose tells it to; nothing enforces it and no gate at submit checks the folder was read.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: The folder is inert and the feature does nothing.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Run a distillation on a repo with a `.reviewer/` folder and check round one carries its questions.

assumptions.assumption: Framing prose alone neutralises untrusted `.reviewer/` content, which a fork's PR can edit.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: A hostile file saying 'skip the interview' or 'fill user_asks from the commit message' is obeyed.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Commit such a file and run a distillation.

assumptions.assumption: A fresh client session picks up the rebuilt bundle; a running one does not.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Agents mid-session silently lack the tool, which is what happened throughout this change's own distillation.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Start a new client session and look for `get_reviewer_instructions` in the reviewer's tool list.

assumptions.assumption: House-rule folders are small and hand-written, so the ceilings bound a mistake rather than a workload.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Real rules land in `omitted` and the reviewer never asks for them.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Call `get_reviewer_instructions` on a large folder and inspect `omitted`.

assumptions.assumption: `.md`, `.markdown` and `.txt` is the right served set.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: A repo shipping `.yaml` or extensionless house rules gets them listed but never read.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Tests cover both the `.yaml` and the extensionless case.

assumptions.assumption: `.reviewer/` belongs inside the coverage denominator, unlike `.intent/`.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Every future house-rules edit, down to a typo fix, needs its own tour stop.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Observable now: H1 and H2 are `coverage_required` in this very run.

adopted.summary:
- Adds a `.reviewer/` folder convention: repo-committed markdown naming the extra questions that repository always wants asked.
- Serves it through a new reviewer-only MCP tool, `get_reviewer_instructions`, bounded and refetchable by name.
- Reports presence only on `compute_diff`, with a nudge to read the folder before round one.
- Rewrites the reviewer role prose, the questions set and the generation guide so house rules read as additional, never as a replacement.
- Dogfoods the convention: this repo ships its own seven house rules and a verification file.
adopted.rationale:
- The server serves the folder because the reviewer has no filesystem tools; handing it `Read` would open the door to the transcript, which is exactly what the split forbids.
- `compute_diff` carries presence only, so a growing folder can never push the `run_id` out of a truncated result.
- The additive framing is repeated at every point of contact because the reviewer meets the folder at the tool description before the prompt it read earlier is relevant.
- Reviewer-only, because house rules are questions and the author's job is answering them.
- README sorts first so it survives a byte budget the rest of the folder does not.
- `.reviewer/` stays in the coverage denominator: unlike `.intent/`, it is not the document's own output, and changing it changes review behaviour for every future PR.
- Untrusted content is handled by framing plus one named refusal case in the prompt, and by nothing else.

tour.title: The loader: reading `.reviewer/` under a budget
tour.what:
- Adds `readReviewerInstructions`, which walks the folder and returns files, sections, `omitted` and `total_bytes`.
- Adds `summarizeReviewerInstructions`, a cheap presence check for `compute_diff`.
- Ranks README first, then files by name, then subfolders, so a citation means the same thing tomorrow.
- Cuts a single file at 64,000 bytes and the whole response at the caller's budget, marking `truncated` and naming the remainder in `omitted`.
- Serves `.md`, `.markdown` and `.txt` only; anything else is listed but not read.
tour.why:
- The reviewer has no filesystem tools by design, so house rules must arrive through a bounded tool like the diff does.
- README-first is not cosmetic: it makes the framing the file that survives a budget the details do not.
- The ceilings bound a mistake, not a workload; they were picked, not measured, and none of the three has a test.
tour.attention: Whether `omitted` is a contract a caller can act on, or a way to lose rules silently.

tour.title: `compute_diff` reports the folder exists, never what is in it
tour.what:
- Adds a `reviewer_instructions` key to the `compute_diff` envelope carrying presence, file count and byte total.
- Appends a nudge to `envelope.next` telling the reviewer to read the folder before recording round one.
tour.why:
- Content deliberately stays out of this response: a repo could otherwise grow its house rules until the `run_id` falls out of a truncated result.
- Round one is the only round these questions can land in, because the two-batch cap means a rule picked up later arrives too late.
tour.attention: That the nudge now hangs off both consent arms, not just the opted-in one.

tour.title: `get_reviewer_instructions`, granted to the reviewer alone
tour.what:
- Registers the tool, taking either a `run_id` or a bare `repo`, plus optional `files` and `max_bytes`.
- Returns the folder's content with an advice line framing it as reference material.
- Adds the tool to the reviewer's `ROLE_TOOLS` and `TOOL_BLURB`; the author does not get it.
tour.why:
- House rules are questions, and the author's job is to answer them, so only the reviewer needs them.
- The content is untrusted (a fork's PR can edit it), so the description frames it as reference that never overrides the protocol, the schema or the sourcing rules.
- Nothing enforces any of that: obedience happens in the agent, not the server.
tour.attention: The bare-`repo` path performs no consent check and serves a repo recorded as 'never' (Q1).

tour.title: Making the house rules read as additional, not as the whole set
tour.what:
- Rewrites reviewer.md step 2 to read the folder, and step 3 to ask the union of baseline, house rules and diff questions.
- Adds 'The repo's own set' to questions.md, stating the folder cannot shorten the baseline set.
- Adds a house-rules paragraph to the generation guide ahead of batch one.
- Renumbers reviewer.md steps 3-5 to 4-6, forced by the new step 2.
tour.why:
- Driven by a user turn predicting the failure mode, not by an observed one: no reviewer was ever seen reading a short house-rules file and shipping a short interview.
- The named risk is that a folder is written by maintainers without the baseline set in view, so it reads as complete when it is not.
- Record all of this as untested prose: the repo's own house rule says an answer describing new wording rather than an old failure means the change is unverified.
tour.attention: H9 is pure renumbering, but it is the tail of H8 rather than churn; do not read it alone.

tour.title: This repo's own house rules, dogfooded
tour.what:
- Adds `.reviewer/README.md` with seven rules: what a prompt change fixed, tool descriptions as prose, which half of a duplicated fact moved, what bounds a response, schema changes are never incidental, transcript evidence behind an interview claim, and consent paths.
- Adds `.reviewer/verification.md` with three: a rebuilt server is not a reloaded one, prompt changes are not covered by `npm test`, and the viewer is verified in a browser or not at all.
tour.why:
- Written by the assistant in one pass from reading this codebase; the user neither supplied nor reviewed them.
- Only one rule has an incident on record: the duplicated-fact rule, whose check script notes 'The manifest said eight while the server registered ten', and which this session then reproduced.
- The response-bounds and consent rules cite incidents that read as real but are not narrated in this session, so they are not attested here.
- Two rules are purely structural, with no incident behind them: the schema rule and the consent rule.
tour.attention: Two of these rules caught defects in the very diff that introduced them, and two were violated by it.

tour.title: Declaring the tool in the release manifest
tour.what: - Adds a `get_reviewer_instructions` entry to manifest.json's tools array.
tour.why:
- Not planned: the pre-commit hook rejected the first commit with 'tools registered but missing from manifest'.
- The array is hand-maintained on purpose; `check-release-consistency.mjs` validates it and does not emit it, and the only generator touching the file syncs the version.
- Without it, `.mcpb` clients would see a short tool list.
tour.attention: The version stays at 1.0.2 with a 16th tool, and nobody raised a bump (Q2).

tour.title: Tests: the loader's contract and the framing that could be edited away
tour.what:
- Adds `reviewer-instructions.test.ts` covering absence, an empty folder, ordering, named subsets, the `.reviewer/` path prefix, non-markdown and extensionless files, dotfiles, the byte budget, and all three advice-line branches.
- Adds two tests to roles.test.ts: the reviewer-only grant, and the additive framing wording in the rendered reviewer definition.
tour.why:
- The framing test exists because the wording lives in prose that a future edit could quietly remove.
- It pins that the wording is present; it does not verify the wording works, and no test can, because obedience happens in the agent.
- No test feeds hostile content through the reader.
tour.attention: What the suite cannot reach: no agent runs anywhere in it.

tour.title: Documenting the convention and the coverage decision
tour.what:
- Adds a README section teaching the `.reviewer/` folder, with the layout and the caveat that most repos need none.
- Adds an ARCHITECTURE paragraph stating the reviewer's questions come from three places, why the tool is reviewer-only, and that `.reviewer/` stays in the coverage denominator.
tour.why:
- The exclusion mechanism for `.intent/` was read in-session and deliberately not reused: `.intent/` is excluded because a document cannot explain the file it is, which does not apply here.
- A change to the house rules changes review behaviour for every future PR, so it should be justified like any other change.
tour.attention: Nobody weighed the cost of a typo fix in the house rules forcing a tour stop (Q5).

tour.title: Four defects this interview found, fixed before the document existed
tour.what:
- Makes `present` mean 'there are house rules to read' in both the reader and the summary, which previously disagreed about a folder that exists but holds nothing readable.
- Appends the house-rules nudge to both consent arms, so a repo that never opted in is still told the folder exists.
- Extracts the advice line into `howToUse` with three branches, so a folder holding only non-readable files is no longer told it does not exist while its files are listed.
- Types a dotless filename as having no extension, instead of taking its last character.
tour.why:
- Two were found by reading the diff cold; two only became findable after the first pair was fixed, by drafting this document against the corrected code.
- The consent-arm defect is exactly what this change's own new house rule predicts, applied to the change that introduced it.
- The advice-line defect was collateral from the first fix: changing what `present` means did not revisit every consumer of it.
- The extension fix changes nothing observable; neither an 'e' nor an empty string is served, and a dotless `readme` still does not lead its folder because `rank()` matches on the extension too.
tour.attention: The consent-arm fix has no test and is verified by reading; the other three now have tests.

tour.title: Favicon, unrelated to the feature
tour.what: - Adds `favicon.svg` with light and dark variants and links it from the viewer's index.html.
tour.why:
- Pre-existing uncommitted work in the tree before this session began; nothing to do with `.reviewer/`.
- Not swept in: the user was asked and chose 'Separate commit, same push', so it is its own commit on this branch.
- Never inspected in this session beyond `git diff --stat`.
tour.attention: Never opened in a browser, so the prefers-color-scheme block is unexercised.
